text:
[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved historical episodes where the tape resembled SPY on 2020-03-16, the median 5-session forward return was 1.36%. The distribution is wide and left-skewed, with a standard deviation of 12.32% and a 10th percentile of -22.12%, meaning that while the typical outcome was slightly positive, severe drawdowns were common in this neighborhood.

[state]
The engine retrieved these analogs because the query state sits at extreme z-scores across almost every feature group. The 5-session return was -12.54% (z=-3) and the 20-session return was -28.95% (z=-3), matching a drawdown from the 60-session peak of -29.11% (z=-3). Realised volatility over 20 sessions was 78.3% (z=3), the VIX sat at 82.69 (z=3), and mean absolute overnight/weekend gaps over 20 sessions were 2.78% (z=3). Dollar volume was historically anomalous at a z-score of 15.408 (z=3). Macro features also hit bounds: WTI crude fell -44.34% over 20 days (z=-3), the trade-weighted USD rose 3.88% (z=3), and the Fed funds target change over 90 days was -1.5 bp (z=-3). These extremes pulled in sessions dominated by early March 2020 and late 2018.

[history]
Across the 50 analogs, the mean 5-session return was -2.3% and the median was 1.36%. The spread is massive, running from -40.53% to 19.93%, with a skew of -1.141. In 56% of the episodes the return was above zero, and in 44% it was below. The bad tail is heavily populated by early March 2020 sessions. Boeing (BA) on 2020-03-05 returned -40.53% over 5 sessions. ConocoPhillips (COP) on 2020-03-04 returned -34.13%. Morgan Stanley (MS) on 2020-03-05 returned -26.49%, and the Energy Select ETF (XLE) on 2020-03-06 returned -24.26%. Bank of America (BAC) on 2020-03-06 returned -6.03%. By contrast, some 2018 episodes bounced: AMD on 2018-12-07 returned 2.26%, and GE on 2019-08-15 returned 2.25%. The closest match was Caterpillar (CAT) on 2020-03-09 at a distance of 0.8076, which went on to lose -10.24%.

[tails]
A position can end near the median and still be un-holdable through the week. The median max adverse excursion across the 50 analogs was -4.21%. At the 10th percentile, the max adverse excursion reached -22.87%, and the 25th percentile was -11.8%. Looking at specific drawdown thresholds, 48% of the analog paths breached a 5% drawdown intra-horizon. A 10% drawdown was breached in 30% of the episodes, a 15% drawdown in 18%, and a 20% drawdown in 14%. On the upside, the median max favourable excursion was 4.68%, with the 75th percentile at 8.58% and the 90th percentile at 11.67%.

[stress]
Of the 14 scenarios run, 5 were skipped because their windows ended after the 5-session embargo before 2020-03-16: covid-crash, rate-shock-2022, regional-banks-2023, carry-unwind-2024, and tariff-shock-2025. Among the executed scenarios, the FOMC decision day scenario produced the worst relative outcome, with a median forward return of -0.52%, a delta of -1.88% versus the baseline, and a 36% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; its caveat is that only 92 decision days exist in the calendar, so the analog set is small and highly overlapping. The earnings release day scenario yielded a median of 0.06% (delta -1.3%), with a 10th percentile of -25.18%; its caveat notes that earnings dates for foreign private issuers come from 6-K full-text search and are noisier than 8-K Item 2.02 dates. The liquidity air pocket scenario matched the baseline median of 1.36% exactly but carried a 10th percentile of -22.12%; its caveat states that gap20 is measured on the underlying exchange session, not a 7x24 venue, and that for the verified tokenized wrapper (SPY/USDT on Bitget), the reference market is closed for 81.4% of the week and 61.18% of realised hourly movement happened in those closed hours. The vol spike scenario actually improved the median to 1.87% (delta 0.51%), though the 10th percentile was -20.12%; its caveat is that VIX shocks mean-revert quickly, stressing entry timing more than terminal value. The fed-tightening-2018 scenario produced a median of 0.89% (delta -0.47%); its caveat is that it ended with a policy pivot in January 2019, which flatters the forward returns of late-window analogs.

[reasoning]
The three most relevant scenarios for this idea are the FOMC decision day (median -0.52%, delta -1.88%, 36% breach probability over 50 analogs) because the query state already features extreme rate-path repricing; the liquidity air pocket (median 1.36%, 30% breach probability over 50 analogs) because the query's 2.78% mean absolute gap and 78.3% volatility directly define this regime; and the vol spike scenario (median 1.87%, delta 0.51%, 30% breach probability over 50 analogs) because the VIX was already at 82.69. A reader should distrust the heavy concentration of early March 2020 dates in the retrieval—multiple symbols like CAT, CVX, BAC, XLE, BA, COP, and MS cluster between 2020-03-04 and 2020-03-09, meaning the left tail is largely one correlated macro event rather than independent draws. No executed scenario contradicts the direction of a slight positive median, though the FOMC scenario shifts it negative.

[limits]
This analysis has concrete limits. As stated in the card's honestVerdict: "Analog retrieval hits its coverage target out of sample and its width tracks each instrument's own volatility, but it is NOT sharper than a same-name unconditional band at matched coverage, and its raw PIT distribution fails a uniformity test. It is a stress-testing and provenance instrument, not an alpha source." The conformal interval achieves 80.8% out-of-sample coverage with a width of 10.4%, but the matched coverage sharpness versus the same-name unconditional benchmark is -7.6%, meaning the engine does not beat a naive baseline when widths are equalized. The directional hit rate is 50.1%.

Regarding path risk, the analog excursion share predicted a mean breach probability of 3.4% at the 10% level, but the realised out-of-sample breach rate was 2%. The calibration gap is 1.4 percentage points with a clustered standard error of 0.48. The analog Brier score MAE was 0.0196. Against the volatility reflection benchmark (0.0241), the paired difference confidence interval [-0.0071, -0.0022] resolves in favor of the analog. Against the same-name calibration (0.024) and pooled calibration (0.021), the intervals [-0.0059, -0.0029] and [-0.0023, -0.0005] also resolve in favor of the analog. However, the PIT chi-square statistic is 208.6 against a 5% critical value of 16.92, confirming the distribution fails uniformity.

The wrapper status is measured. For the primary venue (Bitget RWA perpetual SPY/USDT), the reference cash market is shut for 81.4% of the week, and 61.18% of the wrapper's own hourly movement landed in those shut hours. It is a fair tracker with a return correlation of 0.9477 and a tracking error of 23 bp/day. The basis band is -0.04% to 0.31%, and the spread is 0.13 bps. The caveat is that this is a perpetual carrying funding and idiosyncratic risk, not a redeemable spot token, and the upstream API silently ignores granularity parameters. Across 6 observed weekend blocks, the median weekend return was -0.101%, the 10th percentile was -0.506%, the standard deviation was 0.4191%, and the median intra-weekend adverse excursion was -0.2125%. Zero percent of these 6 weekends breached a 5% drawdown threshold. These are wrapper returns measured while the reference market was shut and are NOT the retrieved outcome distribution above, which is built on 5x24 daily sessions.
